main_text.l: Seruatori debetur gratiarum actio & sacrificium εὐχαριστήριον[?]. Me, inquit Ionas, mirando modo seruauit, & e media morte Deus eripuit. Quare eidem gratias summas me habere æquum est.
Per fidè & voto gratitudinis erga Ser-vatorem Deum nos obstringimus, & il-lud exsolvimus. juxta hæc dicta:
Psal.50.14. Sacrifica Deo laudes, & red de excelso vota tua.
Et versu 23. Qui sacrificat laude, is de-mum glorificat me: qui viam disponit, o-stendam ei salutem Dei.
Philipp.4.6. De nulla re soliciti estote: sed omni in re precibus & supplicatione cum gratiarum actione petitiones vestrae innotescant apud Deum.
Hæc dicta monent, non tantum cordis affectu & linguæ sermone, sed etiam factis seu fidei obedietia, nobis testandam esse gratitudinem.
Pie autem docuit Melanchthon, Gratitudinem complecti veritatem & iusti-ciam[?]. Veritas agnoscit & fatetur, libera-tionem

page.notes: The Greek word in the first paragraph (εὐχαριστήριον) is hard to read at this resolution and is marked [?]. The Greek in the running head is also uncertain. "ciam" in "iusti-ciam" appears to be a printed "tiam" with a worn letter, so it is marked [?]. "soliciti" is uncertain. The opening paragraph has no clear indent and may continue from the previous page, but it starts with a capital and is not marked as a continuation. "Psal." is read from a printed "Pfal." because long s is transcribed as s.
